source: AAA gasprices.aaa.com national average — $4.174 on Sunday June 7, 2026 (Day 100), easing from $4.19 (June 6) and $4.24 (June 4) as crude slipped on US-Iran diplomatic signals and the lowest Chinese crude imports in ten years. Still ~40% above the $2.99 Feb 28 baseline (NBC tracking cites a ~40% rise since the war began). Five states (Alaska, Hawaii, Nevada, Oregon, Washington) remain above $5; California is highest near $5.82. Diesel ~$5.45 (June 1). The May peak $4.536 (May 6, via Fox Business) stayed below AAA's all-time record of $5.016 (set June 14, 2022); pump relief runs 2-3 weeks behind crude. Watson Institute / Costs of War (Brown): Americans have spent ~$318 more per household on gasoline and diesel since the war began (early June, via CBS). ITEP tracker (May 31): cumulative ~$46.5 billion paid extra to the oil industry since Feb 28; additional cost $347.72 per household; summer-end forecast $825.02/household.
